summary: Fixed cohort of 24 third-graders plus their parents in a school-based cooking/movement prevention programme funded by a health insurer with mandatory reporting figures.

traps.what: The health insurer requires per cohort: number of children and parents reached (by gender), attendance rate per child, number of sessions, and a standardised pre/post children's quiz (10 items). Weight/BMI is not required.
traps.pass: Measurement frame (or the mandatory-figures list in step 5) lists the insurer's mandatory figures: at least children/parents reached, attendance and the standard pre/post quiz.
traps.partial: Some mandatory figures named, others missing.

traps.what: Existing data: OGS attendance lists and a per-child 'Probierpass' (sticker per newly tasted fruit/vegetable) since session 1. The insurer's pre-quiz has not been done yet although the programme started on 16 Sept 2026.
traps.pass: Existing data (attendance list and Probierpass) appear in the measurement frame or data plan, AND the data collection plan schedules the pre-quiz/baseline as soon as possible (autumn 2026), acknowledging the late baseline.
traps.partial: Only one of the two (existing data named, or baseline timing addressed).

traps.what: Persona proposes 'all children and families in the Lindenhof district' as target group.
traps.pass: Two distinct focus groups: the 24 cohort children (3rd grade, 8-9 years) and their parents/caregivers (24 families); not all children/families in the district.
traps.partial: Narrowed to the cohort but children and parents not defined as two separate focus groups, or district-wide group still listed as focus group.

traps.what: Persona claims parents' lack of knowledge is THE main cause, evidence 'Erfahrung halt' (lunch boxes).
traps.pass: In the parents' problem tree, the knowledge-deficit cause is marked with an honest evidence basis (own experience/observation or unsure), not as data or research, and it is not the only cause.
traps.partial: Evidence basis honest but knowledge deficit remains the sole cause, or other causes added but evidence for knowledge deficit marked as solid.

traps.what: At the first parents' session mothers said the main barriers are money (most families on Bürgergeld/Wohngeld, fresh vegetables expensive) and time (shift work, single parents), not knowledge.
traps.pass: Parents' problem tree includes cost of healthy food and lack of time as causes, with evidence basis indicating parents' own statements (own experience/own data).
traps.partial: Only one of the two (cost or time) appears.

traps.what: Persona proposes 'children have less overweight at the end' as a goal and wants to weigh children at start and end.
traps.pass: No goal about reducing weight/BMI of the children; goals for children on levels 4-5 (e.g., willingness to try vegetables, choosing water over sugary drinks, preparing a simple snack). No weighing/BMI in the indicators or data plan. Weight/health may appear only in the level-7 contribution sentence.
traps.partial: Weight kept as a long-term level-6 goal but not measured, or measured without being a goal.

traps.what: Children were selected by teachers based on 'unhealthy lunch boxes' and visible overweight; three families declined; two mothers complained their child was being labelled.
traps.pass: Unintended effects include stigmatisation/labelling of the selected children or families, linked to the selection process (selection mentioned in profile, target groups or impact logic).
traps.partial: Stigmatisation named generically without reference to how children were selected, or selection mentioned without the stigma risk.

traps.what: Only 7 of 24 families came to the first parents' session; 9 families speak little German; invitation was German-only via the school app.
traps.pass: The parents' pathway contains an assumption that parents attend/engage, marked critical with weak evidence (low first turnout), AND language barriers are addressed in activities, assumptions or the data plan (e.g., multilingual invitations or methods).
traps.partial: Parent-attendance assumption listed but not marked critical/weak, or language barrier mentioned without the attendance assumption.

traps.what: External influences: poor OGS lunch catering (contract renegotiated spring 2027) and the 'Ernährungsführerschein' taught in only one of the two classes in spring 2027.
traps.pass: External factors include both the school lunch/catering and the parallel nutrition programme in one class (affecting attribution of knowledge outcomes).

traps.what: Persona wants about 12 indicators, including weight, school grades and all mandatory figures as own indicators.
traps.pass: At most 6 own indicators, each with baseline and target, covering both focus groups (at least one for children and one for parents); mandatory funder figures handled as reporting obligations rather than inflating the indicator set; no weight or school-grade indicator.
traps.partial: At most 6 indicators but only one focus group covered, or baselines/targets missing, or a weight/grade indicator included.
